source_text.docs/issues/ISS-0923.yaml: ServiceCatalog.delete/1 only checks ACTIVE process definitions (referencing_active_definitions). After ISS-0917 (PR #2100, on main) a pinned catalog SERVICE_TASK resolves its endpoint from the live service_catalog row or service_catalog_versions; deleting the entry makes pinned in-flight instances go ERROR with service_task_catalog_unresolved/:version_not_found. Decide: block delete while non-terminal instances pin the service, or document. MINOR. Owner ELIXIR-DEV via CODE-DESIGNER. SECURITY-REVIEWER applies (tenant data path).

task.description: WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup in docs/issues/*.yaml) + Step 1 (diagnose), combined. Work in the main checkout C:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-3 on the already-checked-out branch feature/WF03-ISS0923-20261001; do not switch branches. Shared machine: scoped mix tests only, never the full suite. Reproduce against real code (MIX_ENV=test, Postgres up): delete a catalog entry that a non-terminal instance is pinned to and show the instance's service task go ERROR. Determine specifically HOW a pin is queryable: how is the instance's service_catalog version pin recorded (instance projection / pins / process_definition version snapshot), which table(s) and which schema (per-tenant schema vs public; ServiceCatalog.delete/1 is cross-tenant -- see how referencing_active_definitions/2 iterates tenant schemas), what the non-terminal instance statuses are, and whether a cheap tenant-safe query exists. Also check the version-row handling on delete (does delete cascade service_catalog_versions?). Report file:line evidence, the recommended option (block with a typed error like {:error, {:referenced_by_active_instances, ids}} vs document), and its HTTP mapping in the admin router(s) that call delete/1. Do NOT implement the fix and do not edit lib/ or test/. Write your diagnosis into this handoff's result.summary (JSON file) and set status COMPLETED. Do not commit; ORCH commits.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 REGISTRY: no resolved docs/issues entry matches (grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for ServiceCatalog.delete / delete/1; only ISS-0923 itself). Origin is ISS-0917 (resolved, WF03-ISS0917-20261001), design OQ-3 (lib/letflow/design/iss0917-catalog-service-task-pinned-dispatch.md:156,752), which accepted this gap as out of scope. Not a recurrence. Severity stays MINOR.

STEP 1 DIAGNOSIS - REPRODUCED against real code (MIX_ENV=test; throwaway test kept in the session scratchpad, NOT in test/; run with MIX_TEST_PARTITION=923 for an isolated DB, because the shared letflow_test DB holds other sessions' committed tenant_template_build_* registrations that make delete/1 raise 42P01). Sequence: register svc, publish v2 (v1 archived); tenant definition HUMAN_TASK -> SERVICE_TASK(service_id); activate; Engine.create (instance ACTIVE, pinned to v2). Observed output:
  DELETE while definition ACTIVE: {:error, {:referenced_by_active_definitions, [<def id>]}}   (guard only covers ACTIVE definitions)
  Definitions.deprecate(def), then ServiceCatalog.delete(sid) with the instance still ACTIVE -> :ok
  entry rows left: 0; archive rows left: 1   (service_catalog_versions NOT cascaded)
  projection status: active
  Engine.complete_task(HUMAN_TASK) -> {:error, {:instance_execution_error, :service_task_catalog_unresolved, {:node, "svc"}}}
  projection status after: error; events [INSTANCE_STARTED, EXECUTION_ERROR]; EXECUTION_ERROR payload error_type=service_task_catalog_unresolved, details={"reason":"version_not_found"} (a DLQ entry is also written).
Reachable whenever every definition referencing the service leaves ACTIVE (deprecate/archive/superseded) while instances started from it still run, then admin DELETE.

ROOT CAUSE: lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex:880-895 delete/1 gates only on referencing_active_definitions/2 (:940-950; query_referencing_definitions :960-969 filters ProcessDefinition status == :active). It never looks at running instances. Since ISS-0917 the engine resolves a pinned catalog SERVICE_TASK at activation via ServiceCatalog.resolve_pinned_version/3 (service_catalog.ex:567-572), which first calls get_for_tenant/2 on the LIVE service_catalog row (visibility is decided by the live row; archive rows carry no scope/owner, :554-557). No live row -> {:error, :not_found} -> engine maps it to service_task_catalog_unresolved / version_not_found (engine.ex:623, :1199-1207, :3865; engine/service_task.ex:358). Deleting the live row therefore makes EVERY pinned version (live and archived) unresolvable. delete_entry/1 (:904-911) is a bare Repo.delete(entry): no transaction, no lock.

VERSION ROWS: delete/1 does NOT touch service_catalog_versions. Migration priv/repo/migrations/20260921000004_add_service_catalog_versioning.exs:70-93 deliberately has NO FK from service_catalog_versions.service_id (comment :84-90: avoids giving delete/1 a new FK-violation failure mode). Confirmed: 1 orphaned archive row survives a delete; it is unreachable while no live row exists. Untested here: what happens if the same service_id is later re-registered (old archive rows would again match by (service_id, version)); flag for the designer. Existing test helper cleanup_entry! deletes both tables manually (test/letflow/engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:61-64).

HOW A PIN IS QUERYABLE (all per-tenant schema, NOT public; service_catalog and service_catalog_versions are the public-schema tables):
 1. Authoritative pin is event-sourced: INSTANCE_STARTED payload.pinned_versions (engine.ex:1894-1899), a list of %{kind:"catalog_entry", ref: service_id, resolved_id: version_id, version, source}; INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND events amend it (PinResolver.reconstruct_effective_pins/2, pin_resolver.ex:643-676). Observed payload: [{"kind":"catalog_entry","ref":"iss0923-svc-131","resolved_id":"<uuid>","source":"resolved","version":"2"},{"kind":"variable_schema",...}]. NOT cheap to query: events/events_archive have no jsonb index on payload, reconstruction walks the full log, and no projection column carries pins.
 2. CHEAP, tenant-safe superset: tenant-schema instance_projections (EventStore.InstanceProjection; status Ecto.Enum active/completed/cancelled/error; PK instance_id) JOIN tenant-schema instance_definition_snapshots (Definitions.InstanceDefinitionSnapshot; PK instance_id; graph jsonb; write-once; one row per instance) on instance_id, WHERE projection status is non-terminal AND the snapshot graph has a SERVICE_TASK node with attributes.service_id = service_id. This is the same jsonb_array_elements/EXISTS fragment already in @service_task_reference_fragment (service_catalog.ex:952-958), pointed at the snapshot graph instead of process_definitions.graph. I ran this probe in the repro (raw SQL, schema-qualified, status IN ('ACTIVE','ERROR'), service_id bound as $2) and it returned [["ACTIVE", 4]] for the pinned instance. Why a graph match is a valid proxy for the pin: PinResolver extracts ("SERVICE_TASK","service_id") -> :catalog_entry refs from the graph at start (pin_resolver.ex ~:307) so every referenced service_id is pinned; a rebind changes the version, never the ref. The over-approximation (a graph node never reached still blocks) errs on the safe side.
 3. Cross-tenant iteration: reuse the shape of referencing_active_definitions/2 (service_catalog.ex:940-950): TenantProvisioning.list_registrations/0, Repo.all(query, prefix: registration.schema_name), reject empties. A sibling private fn (e.g. referencing_non_terminal_instances/1) has the same shape. No migration/index is needed: idx_proj_status is a PARTIAL index WHERE status='ACTIVE' (migration 20260816120003), so ACTIVE rows are index-assisted, ERROR rows are scanned; acceptable, same stated per-tenant-loop cost as REQ-191 design OQ-2.
 4. Non-terminal statuses: InstanceProjection.terminal?/1 (instance_projection.ex:223-225): terminal = :completed, :cancelled only; :active and :error are NON-terminal (the repro's instance ends in :error). Recommend the guard use 'not terminal?' = [:active, :error] so there is one authoritative definition. Designer must decide explicitly whether ERROR instances block (an instance in ERROR for another reason may be retried/resumed and would then hit the same failure; an ERROR instance already stuck on this pin would block deletion until cancelled, which is the admin escape hatch).

RECOMMENDED OPTION: BLOCK, not merely document. Add a second guard to delete/1 after the active-definition guard: if any tenant has a non-terminal instance whose snapshot graph references the service_id, return {:error, {:referenced_by_active_instances, ids}} (or grouped per tenant like reference_conflict()), no write. Rationale: the pinning contract (PIN-01..04, ISS-0917 'no fallback, ever') promises in-flight instances keep their pinned version; delete/1 silently breaking it contradicts that; cost is one extra read-only loop. Documentation-only would leave a data-integrity trap with no admin visibility. Order: :not_found first, then the existing definitions check, then the instances check. Update delete/1's @doc and @spec union (service_catalog.ex:870-879). The TOCTOU window (instance started between check and delete) is the same accepted window the existing definition guard has; a start needs an ACTIVE definition that the first guard already blocks, so it is narrow; designer should state it.
 Optional, designer decision: delete the service's service_catalog_versions rows in the same delete (Repo.transaction / Ecto.Multi) so no orphaned archive rows remain (safe once the new guard guarantees no live pins).
 Related but OUT of scope: update_scope/2 narrowing (:835-850) has the same blind spot (only active definitions of other tenants, not their running instances); ORCH may want a follow-up issue.

HTTP MAPPING: the only caller of delete/1 is lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex handle_delete (:274-288), DELETE /admin/services/:service_id (grep of lib/: only admin_services.ex and service_catalog.ex). Its case has NO catch-all, so an unhandled new error tuple raises CaseClauseError (INV-8 bare crash): the new clause is mandatory. Add {:error, {:referenced_by_active_instances, ids}} -> Response.send_problem(conn, Error.service_referenced_by_active_instances(ids)), with a new constructor in lib/letflow/api/error.ex beside service_referenced_by_active_definitions/1 (:428-437): HTTP 409, type @problems_base <> "service-referenced-by-active-instances", title "Service Referenced By Active Instances", extensions %{"instance_ids" => ids} (or per-tenant conflicts). Designer should grep docs/ and any openapi for 'service-referenced-by-active-definitions' to update the documented DELETE responses.

SECURITY NOTES (SECURITY-REVIEWER applies): (a) the endpoint is platform-admin cross-tenant and already returns cross-tenant definition ids, so instance ids are the same exposure class, but they can be numerous: cap the list (first N ids + total count) to bound response size; (b) schema prefix must come only from TenantProvisioning registrations, never request input, as in the existing loop; (c) query must stay parameterised (service_id bound with ^), no interpolation of schema or service_id into SQL strings; (d) confirm the route stays admin-only.

WHY EXISTING TESTS MISSED IT: test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs covers delete only for active-definition blocking, not-found and the concurrent-delete race; engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs (ISS-0917) exercises unresolved pins via rebind to a missing version (T4b) and a non-visible tenant (T6), never by deleting the live row. ISS-0917 explicitly deferred it (OQ-3).

TEST HINTS for TEST-DESIGNER (fail-first must discriminate, per WF-03): committed-row test (Sandbox.mode :auto, async: false, as engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:47-50) with provisioned_tenant!. Cases: (1) pinned ACTIVE instance + deprecated definition -> typed error, live row and archive rows intact; (2) same after instance COMPLETED/CANCELLED -> :ok; (3) ERROR-state instance per designer decision; (4) tenant-scoped service pinned by an instance in tenant A is still seen (cross-tenant loop); (5) a DIFFERENT service_id's pinned instance does not block (guards substring/LIKE over-match); (6) HTTP 409 body shape in the admin_services router test. Mutants: drop the status filter (terminal instance wrongly blocks); substring match on service_id; query only the first tenant schema.

ENV NOTES: (1) the shared DB letflow_test (port 5472, container letflow-2-postgres-1) contains stale/in-flight tenant_template_build_* rows in tenant_schemas from concurrent sessions; ServiceCatalog.delete/1 iterates ALL registrations and raised Postgrex 42P01 on one whose schema did not exist (service_catalog.ex:943-947). Not this issue's defect, but a hazard for the new loop and for any delete test; use MIX_TEST_PARTITION=<n> for an isolated DB. (2) I created database letflow_test923 on letflow-2-postgres-1 for the repro; my DROP DATABASE was backgrounded (task bi2ibav1n) and may not have completed; harmless, can be dropped later. (3) No file under lib/ or test/ was edited: git status --porcelain lib test was empty after the run. Nothing committed.
issues: MINOR: delete/1 ignores non-terminal instances pinned to the service (reproduced); recommended fix = typed block {:error,{:referenced_by_active_instances,ids}} mapped to HTTP 409

Open design questions for CODE-DESIGNER: (a) do :error instances block (recommend not terminal? = active+error); (b) cascade-delete service_catalog_versions in the same transaction; (c) cap/shape of the returned id list
Related out-of-scope gap: update_scope/2 narrowing has the same blind spot for running instances of other tenants
Env hazard: delete/1 iterates all tenant_schemas registrations and raised 42P01 on a stale tenant_template_build_* row in the shared test DB; use MIX_TEST_PARTITION for tests
